tagline: Connecting for good while transforming our business.
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the primary driver of BT's strategic transformation: the rollout of the full fibre network is at the core of its future value, with leverage effects on quality, reliability, and residential and business revenues. More than 50% of UK homes and businesses now have access to faster, more reliable broadband.
company_description: BT Group is a major telecommunications services provider in the United Kingdom, offering fixed, mobile, and internet connectivity solutions to consumers and businesses. It plays a central role in the country's digital infrastructure.

kpis.name: Fibre Coverage (premises)
kpis.explanation: Number of buildings connected or eligible for Openreach's ultra-fast full fibre network.
kpis.description: Openreach is expanding its full fibre network at a sustained pace, enabling more than half of UK homes and businesses to access faster, more reliable broadband.
kpis.signal: More than 50% of UK homes and businesses now have access to full fibre thanks to Openreach investments.

kpis.name: 5G Population Coverage
kpis.explanation: Percentage of the UK population covered by the BT/EE 5G network.
kpis.description: 5G coverage reaches 75% nationwide, with peaks of 77% in England and only 29% in Northern Ireland.
kpis.signal: Rapid expansion of the 5G network, despite significant regional disparities.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: BT's consolidated revenue for the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Revenue declined to £20.4 billion (FY25), compared to £20.8 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Revenue down 2% in FY25, reflecting competitive and market pressures.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted gross operating income, excluding exceptional items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA increased to £8.2 billion (FY25), compared to £8.1 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Slight improvement in operating profitability (+1%) despite revenue decline.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.description: Capital expenditures remained stable at £4.9 billion in FY25, identical to FY24. BT is the largest UK infrastructure investor in the FTSE 100, with £24.3 billion invested over 5 years.
kpis.signal: Stable investment at £4.9 billion, reflecting continued fibre deployment.

kpis.name: Normalized Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after capital expenditures and adjustments.
kpis.description: Normalized free cash flow increased significantly to £1.6 billion in FY25, compared to £1.3 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Significant cash flow improvement (+23%), demonstrating progress toward targets of £2bn in FY27 and £3bn in FY30.

kpis.name: Number of Mobile Sites
kpis.explanation: Total number of mobile telephony sites operated by BT.
kpis.description: BT operates approximately 19,500 mobile sites across the United Kingdom.
kpis.signal: Extensive mobile network spanning approximately 19,500 sites.

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated by operating activities before capital expenditures.
kpis.description: Operating cash flow reached £7.0 billion in FY25, up 17% compared to £6.0 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Strong improvement in operating cash generation.

kpis.name: Profit Before Tax
kpis.description: Profit before tax amounted to £1.3 billion in FY25, up 8% compared to £1.2 billion in FY24.
kpis.signal: Improved net profitability despite revenue decline.

kpis.name: Basic Earnings Per Share
kpis.description: Earnings per share reached 10.8 pence in FY25, up 24% compared to 8.7 pence in FY24.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Dividend paid to shareholders per ordinary share.
kpis.description: Dividend per share amounted to 8.16 pence for FY25, reflecting BT's commitment to delivering shareholder value while continuing to invest in future growth.
kpis.signal: Progressive dividend policy maintained with a 2% increase for FY25.

kpis.name: Group Net Promoter Score
kpis.explanation: Customer satisfaction and loyalty indicator measured by Net Promoter Score.
kpis.description: Group NPS improved from 24.8 in FY24 to 29.5 in FY25, reflecting efforts to place customers at the heart of decision-making.
kpis.signal: Substantial improvement in customer satisfaction following increased focus on customer experience.

kpis.name: Employee Engagement

kpis.description: 82% of employees feel positive about developing new ways to serve customers and are empowered to make decisions, according to the 'Your Say' survey. This score exceeds the UK benchmark by 8%.
kpis.signal: Very high engagement level, 8% above the UK benchmark.

kpis.description: BT Group added more than £22.8 billion to the UK economy, connecting people, businesses, and society.

risks.title: Dependence on Ofcom Regulation and Regulatory Uncertainty
risks.summary: BT depends heavily on Ofcom regulatory decisions for the profitability of its massive infrastructure investments (£24.3bn over 5 years). Ofcom's Telecoms Access Review determines return on investment conditions and pricing predictability. Changes in regulatory policy (shift from 'CPI+' to 'pounds and pence') directly impact customer billing and margins.
risks.score_rationale: Risk highlighted in the CEO and Chairman's letter (pages 3-4, 7). Intensive language: 'key priority,' 'long-term certainty and predictability.' Stable but critical trend: Ofcom Telecoms Access Review launched in FY25 determines future investment returns. Very high category weight: sector regulation determines the viability of BT's business model.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Growing Digital Threats
risks.summary: BT operates the UK's most critical networks and faces increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. The group blocks 2 million potential cyber-attacks daily and tens of millions of fraudulent calls/SMS. Risks include attacks on critical infrastructure, customer data theft, and service interruptions affecting the national economy.
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly raised by the CEO (page 7): 'digital safety,' 'stopping two million potential cyber-attacks every day,' 'quantum' technologies. Intensive language: '24/7 threats,' 'increasingly sophisticated.' Upward trend: mention of cutting-edge technologies (quantum) indicates threat escalation. Critical category weight for critical network operator.

risks.title: Intense Competition in Fixed and Mobile Connectivity
risks.summary: BT faces intense competition from Virgin Media, Sky, Vodafone, and other operators in fixed and mobile markets. The group lost Consumer customers for 3 years before stabilizing in FY25. Differentiation relies on network quality (EE best mobile network 11 consecutive years) and innovation (Wi-Fi 7, 5G Standalone).
risks.score_rationale: Implicit but major risk: CEO mentions 'return to growth' and 'stabilise our consumer base' (page 7), indicating competitive pressures. Moderate language but clear context: historical customer losses over 3 years before stabilization. Stable but structural trend. High category weight: saturated UK market with Virgin Media, Sky, Vodafone.

risks.title: Operational Complexity and Transformation Risks
risks.summary: BT is executing a major transformation: migration of 1.2m customers from legacy PSTN network, headcount reduction from ~100k to 75-90k, consolidation from 300 sites to 30 hubs. Execution risks include service interruptions, customer losses during migrations, and restructuring costs. Three new leaders appointed in FY25 to lead this transformation.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk raised by CEO (pages 5-8): 'radically simplify and digitalise,' migration of 1.2m customers from legacy PSTN network, reduction from 300 to 30 sites. Intensive language: 'scale of BT's modernisation agenda,' 'essential we have the right management team.' Upward trend: accelerated transformation underway. High category weight: 5-year execution risk.

risks.title: Dependence on Massive Fibre Infrastructure Investments
risks.summary: BT invests £4.9bn annually in capex (higher than peers) to build 18m+ homes with full fibre and expand 5G. Risks include: cost overruns, construction delays, insufficient customer adoption, and dependence on regulatory stability to justify returns. 20% increase in build rate in FY26 amplifies these risks.
risks.score_rationale: Structural risk: CEO highlights 'largest investor in UK infrastructure' (page 7), £4.9bn annual capex, target of 30m premises with full fibre by 2030. Intensive language: 'sustained peak levels of investment.' Upward trend: 20% increase in build rate in FY26. High category weight: capex-intensive, long-term returns.

risks.title: Dependence on Technology Suppliers and Key Partners
risks.summary: BT depends on major technology partners for innovation (Wi-Fi 7, 5G Standalone, quantum security). Supply disruptions or changes in supplier strategies could impact the ability to innovate and maintain competitive advantage. Risk amplified by the complexity of global supply chains.
risks.score_rationale: Implicit risk: CEO mentions 'partnerships with the world's best technology providers' (page 7) and 'Global Fabric' (world-first platform). Moderate language but clear dependence. Stable trend. Moderate category weight: BT depends on suppliers for innovation (Wi-Fi 7, 5G, quantum).

risks.title: Critical Services Risks and Societal Responsibility
risks.summary: BT operates critical services (Emergency Services Network, government) and faces growing expectations for digital inclusion and child protection. Risks include: critical service failures, digital exclusion, exposure to harmful content for minors. Emergency Services Network contract extended 7 years indicates public sector dependence.
risks.score_rationale: Emerging risk: CEO highlights 'custodians of some of the country's most iconic brands' and 'digital inclusion' (pages 7-8). Moderate language but growing responsibility. Upward trend: increased commitment to digital inclusion, child safety. Moderate category weight: reputational and regulatory risk.

risks.title: Asset Impairment and Future Depreciation Risks
risks.summary: BT is massively migrating from legacy PSTN network to fibre/5G, creating risk of legacy asset impairment and future depreciation charges. Product portfolio simplification and site consolidation (300 to 30) may generate impairment charges. Risk amplified by transformation acceleration.
risks.score_rationale: Implicit risk: massive migration from legacy PSTN (1.2m customers) and product simplification suggest legacy asset depreciation. Moderate language but clear context. Upward trend: accelerated legacy migration. Moderate category weight: accounting and balance sheet risk.

ai_positioning.summary: BT does not appear as a leader in generative AI. Its positioning focuses on network infrastructure (fibre, 5G) and connectivity as the foundation of the digital economy, with no direct mention of AI products or services in the 2025 annual report.
evidence: No mention of generative AI or AI APIs in the provided report excerpt.
Priority focus on connectivity, full fibre, and 5G as growth and transformation drivers.
No references to AI partnerships or AI offerings for businesses or consumers in the analyzed sections.
The report emphasizes operational transformation, customer experience, and physical infrastructure.
